reviewers.summary: The fixture, ambiguity path, hostile document actions, and script-specific review assertions are covered. M-09’s required same-harness valid-claim control is absent, so the tests do not prove that a valid claim still produces a request under the script case’s setup.

findingList.message: M-09 is missing the valid-claim control under the script case’s setup. Keep the default witness page valid, add the script text to a separate Case B page, then assess the default claim against the same current basis and assert Request, exactly one inbox request, and exactly one receipt.

evidence.codePathTraced: M09 assesses the script claim after replacing its witness page with the script text. It never assesses the default claim against that same current basis and StateHarness.
evidence.failureScenario: If assessment incorrectly returns Review for the valid default claim on that basis, the test still passes. M-09 requires the script text on a separate document page, then the valid default claim to produce Request with exactly one inbox request and receipt in the same harness.

reviewers.summary: The fixture and adversarial tests cover the other listed behaviors. M-09 remains incomplete because its valid-claim control uses a separate harness and basis.

findingList.message: M-09's script check lacks the required valid-claim control under the same setup. Add the script text to a separate Case B document page, assess the script claim first, then assess the default valid claim in the same StateHarness and assert Request with exactly one inbox request and one receipt.

evidence.codePathTraced: The script claim is assessed with a StateHarness whose llp-history-gap document has been replaced by the script text. The valid-claim control runs later through a separate endpoint harness with a different basis.
evidence.failureScenario: If assessment returns Review for valid claims under the script test's modified basis, the endpoint control still passes because it assesses a claim against a separate, unmodified basis. M-09 requires both claims to be assessed in the same harness against the same complete, unambiguous basis, with the script text on a separate document page.

reviewers.summary: I found no concrete security vulnerability in the changed code. The script-claim check matches the exact shape required by the issue, and the added tests exercise the Case B instruction and cross-case access paths.
